html:
The Battle of Gettysburg was fought from 1 to 3 July 1863 at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, United States. The Union army of General George Meade beat the Confederate army of Robert E. Lee. It was the largest battle of the American Civil War, with about 50,000 men killed, wounded or missing.

After a victory in Virginia in May, Lee invaded the North a second time. He hoped a win on Northern soil would push the North to make peace. He had about 75,000 men and Meade about 90,000. The armies met by chance. On the first day the Confederates drove Union troops through the town onto hills to the south. On the second day they attacked both ends of the Union line and failed. On the third day Lee sent about 12,500 men across open fields at the Union centre. This attack, Pickett's Charge, was shot to pieces. Lee retreated to Virginia.

He never invaded the North again. With the fall of Vicksburg the next day, Gettysburg marked the turn of the war against the Confederacy. In November Abraham Lincoln gave the Gettysburg Address at a new cemetery there, on "government of the people, by the people, for the people".
